parsed.study_design: Descriptive, empirical, qualitative household survey study supplemented by government-official interviews
parsed.population_and_sample: 150 households across 13 subwards in Buguruni, Ilala, and Magomeni wards, Dar es Salaam, plus interviews with officials from the Ministry of Water, DAWASCO, TANESCO, and ward/subward administrations
parsed.exposure: Institutional and administrative conditions of water provision, including DAWASCO rationing and delivery schedules, kiosk and well operating practices, connection costs, electricity interruptions, and regulatory oversight
parsed.outcome: Household water availability and reliability, method of access, consumption quantity, fetching and waiting burdens, affordability, service interruptions, and reliance on backup sources
parsed.rationale: The Research Methodology section (p. 5) identifies a survey of 150 households and interviews with water, electricity, and local-government officials. The Research Findings and Tables 1–2 (pp. 6–9) empirically connect DAWASCO rationing, kiosk administration, and electricity-dependent provision to household water availability, reliability, and access method. The impacts sections (pp. 10–12) report reduced consumption, altered routines, longer collection times, and reliance on less desirable backup sources.
